t: Obat ini harus ditebus dengan resep dokter di apotek.
e: This medicine has to be filled with a doctor's prescription at the pharmacy.
g: Obat resep = prescription medicine: harus ditebus dengan resep = must be filled with a prescription.

t: Obat warung biasanya cukup untuk sakit kepala ringan seperti ini.
e: Corner-stall medicine is usually enough for a mild headache like this.
g: Obat warung = cheap over-the-counter meds from corner stalls, sold per strip — no resep needed.

t: Apoteker menjelaskan aturan pakai obat ini dengan sangat sabar.
e: The pharmacist explains this medicine's directions for use very patiently.

t: Sirup obat batuk ini harus dikocok dulu sebelum diminum.
e: This cough syrup has to be shaken first before being drunk.
g: Dulu after a verb = 'first': dikocok dulu sebelum diminum = shaken first before drinking.

t: Anak saya lebih suka obat sirup daripada tablet karena rasanya manis.
e: My child prefers syrup medicine to tablets because it tastes sweet.

t: Salep ini dioleskan tipis-tipis pada kulit yang gatal dua kali sehari.
e: This ointment is applied thinly on the itchy skin twice a day.
g: Doubling an adjective = 'in that manner': dioleskan tipis-tipis = spread on thinly.

t: Minum tablet ini sesudah makan supaya lambung kamu tidak perih.
e: Take this tablet after eating so your stomach doesn't sting.

t: Jangan melebihi dosis yang tertulis di kemasan obat itu.
e: Don't exceed the dose written on that medicine's packaging.

t: Apotek dekat rumah kami buka dua puluh empat jam setiap hari.
e: The pharmacy near our house is open twenty-four hours every day.

t: Saya perlu membeli vitamin dan obat tetes mata di apotek.
e: I need to buy vitamins and eye drops at the pharmacy.

t: Obat ini bisa membuat kamu mengantuk, jadi jangan menyetir setelah meminumnya.
e: This medicine can make you drowsy, so don't drive after taking it.

t: Kalau demamnya tidak turun dalam tiga hari, segera periksakan ke dokter.
e: If the fever doesn't go down in three days, have it checked by a doctor right away.
g: Periksakan = have it checked: periksakan ke dokter = take it to the doctor. The -kan asks it done.

t: Apoteker menyarankan obat generik karena harganya jauh lebih murah.
e: The pharmacist recommends the generic medicine because its price is much cheaper.
g: Obat generik = generic medicine, same content but cheaper: minta obat generik = ask for the generic.

t: Simpan sirup ini di kulkas setelah botolnya dibuka pertama kali.
e: Store this syrup in the fridge after the bottle is opened for the first time.

t: Ibu selalu menyimpan kotak obat kecil di lemari dapur untuk keadaan darurat.
e: Mom always keeps a small medicine box in the kitchen cupboard for emergencies.

t: Obat alergi ini hanya boleh diminum satu tablet per hari.
e: This allergy medicine may only be taken one tablet per day.

t: Saya lupa membawa resep, jadi apoteker tidak bisa memberikan obatnya.
e: I forgot to bring the prescription, so the pharmacist can't hand over the medicine.

t: Tolong tuliskan aturan pakai di label supaya nenek tidak bingung.
e: Please write the directions for use on the label so Grandma doesn't get confused.

t: Tolong panggil ambulans, ayah saya tiba-tiba jatuh pingsan di kamar mandi!
e: Please call an ambulance, my father suddenly fainted in the bathroom!
g: Tolong + verb = please (asking for help): tolong panggil ambulans = please call an ambulance.

t: Pasien kecelakaan itu langsung dibawa ke UGD rumah sakit terdekat.
e: That accident patient was taken straight to the ER of the nearest hospital.
g: UGD (Unit Gawat Darurat) = the ER; many hospitals label it IGD instead. Ke UGD = to the ER.

t: Perawat di IGD memeriksa tekanan darah dan denyut nadi saya.
e: The nurse in the ER checks my blood pressure and pulse.

t: Nomor darurat di Indonesia adalah seratus dua belas, mudah diingat.
e: The emergency number in Indonesia is one hundred twelve, easy to remember.
g: 112 is Indonesia's general emergency number: nomor darurat = emergency number.

t: Luka di dahinya cukup dalam sehingga harus dijahit lima jahitan.
e: The wound on his forehead is quite deep, so it has to be closed with five stitches.

t: Adik saya keracunan makanan laut dan muntah-muntah sepanjang malam.
e: My younger sibling got food poisoning from seafood and kept vomiting all night.

t: Dokter jaga memasang infus karena pasien itu kekurangan cairan.
e: The doctor on duty puts in an IV drip because that patient lacks fluids.

t: Jangan panik, tekan lukanya dengan kain bersih sampai pendarahan berhenti.
e: Don't panic, press the wound with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops.

t: Golongan darah saya O, jadi saya sering diminta mendonorkan darah.
e: My blood type is O, so I'm often asked to donate blood.

t: Kalau ada kebakaran, jangan memakai lift, turunlah lewat tangga darurat.
e: If there's a fire, don't use the elevator; go down via the emergency stairs.
g: -lah softens a command: turunlah lewat tangga = do go down the stairs.

t: Suami saya menelepon ambulans sambil menenangkan anak-anak yang ketakutan.
e: My husband calls the ambulance while calming the frightened children.

t: Petugas UGD bertanya obat apa saja yang sedang diminum pasien.
e: The ER staff asks what medicines the patient is currently taking.

t: Untung ada tetangga yang mengantar kami ke rumah sakit tengah malam.
e: Luckily there was a neighbor who drove us to the hospital in the middle of the night.
g: Untung at the start of a sentence = luckily: untung ada tetangga = luckily there was a neighbor.

t: Dia tersedak bakso, untung temannya tahu cara menolongnya.
e: He choked on a meatball; luckily his friend knew how to help him.

t: Sebelum ambulans datang, baringkan pasien dan longgarkan kerah bajunya.
e: Before the ambulance arrives, lay the patient down and loosen his shirt collar.

t: Kepalanya terbentur pintu mobil, sekarang dia merasa mual dan pusing.
e: His head hit the car door; now he feels nauseous and dizzy.

t: Adik menangis keras waktu disuntik di lengan kirinya.
e: My little sibling cries loudly when injected in his left arm.

t: Keluarga pasien menunggu dengan cemas di depan ruang operasi.
e: The patient's family waits anxiously in front of the operating room.

t: Sejak pagi saya merasa mual dan tidak nafsu makan sama sekali.
e: Since morning I have felt nauseous and have no appetite at all.

t: Nenek mengeluh sesak napas setiap kali naik tangga ke lantai dua.
e: Grandma complains of shortness of breath every time she climbs the stairs to the second floor.
g: Mengeluh = to complain (of): mengeluh sesak napas = complains of shortness of breath.

t: Saya alergi udang, wajah saya langsung bengkak sesudah memakannya.
e: I am allergic to shrimp; my face swells up right after eating it.

t: Kulit saya gatal dan muncul bintik merah setelah meminum obat baru itu.
e: My skin is itchy and red spots appeared after I took that new medicine.

t: Tenggorokan saya kering dan suara saya hampir hilang sejak kemarin.
e: My throat is dry and my voice has almost disappeared since yesterday.

t: Badan saya lemas dan kepala saya pusing seperti berputar.
e: My body is weak and my head is dizzy, like it's spinning.
g: Pusing covers both dizzy and stressed-out: kepala saya pusing = my head is spinning.

t: Anak itu demam tinggi dan menggigil meskipun sudah memakai selimut tebal.
e: That child has a high fever and is shivering even though he's already using a thick blanket.

t: Dokter bertanya sudah berapa lama saya merasakan nyeri di dada.
e: The doctor asks how long I have been feeling pain in my chest.

t: Perut saya kembung dan mulas setelah makan pedas semalam.
e: My stomach is bloated and crampy after eating spicy food last night.
g: Kembung = bloated, full of gas: perut kembung = a bloated belly.

t: Mata saya merah dan berair, mungkin karena debu di jalan.
e: My eyes are red and watery, maybe because of the dust on the road.

t: Dia batuk berdahak sudah seminggu, sebaiknya dia segera ke dokter.
e: He has had a phlegmy cough for a week already; he had better go to the doctor soon.

t: Telinga kanan saya berdenging sejak turun dari pesawat tadi malam.
e: My right ear has been ringing since I got off the plane last night.

t: Tekanan darah ayah naik lagi karena dia lupa meminum obatnya.
e: Dad's blood pressure went up again because he forgot to take his medicine.

t: Saya sulit tidur karena hidung tersumbat dan kepala terasa berat.
e: I have trouble sleeping because my nose is blocked and my head feels heavy.

t: Lutut saya bengkak setelah jatuh dari sepeda kemarin sore.
e: My knee is swollen after I fell off my bicycle yesterday afternoon.

t: Napasnya berbunyi seperti siulan, mungkin asmanya kambuh lagi.
e: His breathing sounds like whistling; maybe his asthma is flaring up again.
g: Kambuh = (an illness) flares up again: asmanya kambuh = his asthma is back.

t: Setiap musim hujan, alergi dingin saya kambuh dan kulit jadi gatal.
e: Every rainy season my cold allergy flares up and my skin gets itchy.

t: Dia mengalami mimisan tiba-tiba, mungkin karena cuaca terlalu panas.
e: He suddenly got a nosebleed, maybe because the weather is too hot.

t: Kartu BPJS saya tertinggal di rumah, untung ada versi digitalnya.
e: My BPJS card was left at home; luckily there is a digital version of it.
g: BPJS = Indonesia's national health insurance; nearly everyone carries the kartu BPJS = BPJS card.

t: Untuk berobat murah, warga biasanya datang dulu ke puskesmas dekat rumah.
e: For cheap medical treatment, residents usually go first to the puskesmas near their homes.
g: Puskesmas (pusat kesehatan masyarakat) = community health center, the cheap first stop for care.

t: Petugas puskesmas meminta saya mengambil nomor antrean di mesin.
e: The puskesmas staff asks me to take a queue number at the machine.

t: Tanpa surat rujukan dari puskesmas, BPJS tidak menanggung biaya rumah sakit.
e: Without a referral letter from the puskesmas, BPJS doesn't cover the hospital costs.
g: BPJS is tiered: you need a surat rujukan (referral letter) from the puskesmas before the hospital.

t: Ibu rutin memeriksakan gula darahnya di puskesmas setiap awal bulan.
e: Mom routinely has her blood sugar checked at the puskesmas at the start of every month.

t: Iuran BPJS keluarga kami dibayar otomatis lewat aplikasi bank.
e: Our family's BPJS premiums are paid automatically through the bank app.
g: Iuran = a regular membership fee: iuran BPJS = the monthly BPJS premium.

t: Antrean di puskesmas pagi ini panjang sekali sampai ke halaman.
e: The queue at the puskesmas this morning is really long, all the way to the yard.

t: Dokter puskesmas merujuk saya ke dokter spesialis kulit di rumah sakit.
e: The puskesmas doctor refers me to a skin specialist at the hospital.

t: Bidan di puskesmas memeriksa kandungan kakak saya setiap bulan.
e: The midwife at the puskesmas examines my older sister's pregnancy every month.

t: Anak-anak mendapat imunisasi gratis di posyandu dekat balai desa.
e: The children get free immunizations at the posyandu near the village hall.
g: Posyandu = neighborhood health post: monthly weigh-ins and shots for kids. Di posyandu = at the post.

t: Kelas BPJS menentukan jenis kamar rawat inap yang kamu dapat.
e: Your BPJS tier determines the type of inpatient room you get.

t: Saya harus memperbarui data alamat supaya kartu BPJS tetap aktif.
e: I have to update my address data so my BPJS card stays active.

t: Obat dari puskesmas gratis, kita hanya perlu menunjukkan kartu berobat.
e: Medicine from the puskesmas is free; we only need to show our patient card.

t: Puskesmas keliling datang ke kampung kami setiap hari Rabu pagi.
e: The mobile puskesmas comes to our neighborhood every Wednesday morning.

t: Pak RT membantu mengurus kartu BPJS untuk warga yang belum punya.
e: The neighborhood chief helps arrange BPJS cards for residents who don't have one yet.

t: Gigi geraham saya berlubang dan sakitnya menjalar sampai ke telinga.
e: My molar has a cavity and the pain spreads all the way to my ear.
g: Menjalar = (pain) spreads, creeps: sakitnya menjalar ke telinga = the pain spreads to the ear.

t: Dokter gigi menyarankan gigi itu ditambal sebelum lubangnya makin besar.
e: The dentist suggests that tooth be filled before the cavity gets bigger.

t: Anak saya takut sekali setiap kali diajak ke dokter gigi.
e: My child is really scared every time he is taken to the dentist.

t: Gigi bungsunya harus dicabut karena tumbuh miring dan menekan gigi lain.
e: His wisdom tooth has to be pulled because it grows crooked and presses on the other teeth.
g: Gigi bungsu = wisdom tooth, literally 'youngest-child tooth': dicabut = gets pulled.

t: Setelah gigi dicabut, jangan berkumur terlalu keras selama satu hari.
e: After the tooth is pulled, don't rinse your mouth too hard for one day.

t: Saya membersihkan karang gigi di klinik setiap enam bulan sekali.
e: I get my tartar cleaned at the clinic once every six months.

t: Adik memakai behel, jadi setiap bulan dia ke dokter gigi untuk kontrol.
e: My younger sibling wears braces, so every month she goes to the dentist for a checkup.

t: Gusi saya berdarah setiap kali menyikat gigi terlalu kencang.
e: My gums bleed every time I brush my teeth too hard.

t: Dokter gigi memuji anak saya karena rajin menggosok gigi sebelum tidur.
e: The dentist praises my child for diligently brushing his teeth before bed.

t: Biaya menambal satu gigi di klinik swasta lumayan mahal.
e: The cost of filling one tooth at a private clinic is pretty expensive.

t: Mata minus saya bertambah karena terlalu sering menatap layar ponsel.
e: My nearsightedness has gotten worse because I stare at my phone screen too often.
g: Mata minus = nearsighted, said with the number: minus saya bertambah = my prescription got worse.

t: Petugas optik memeriksa mata saya dengan mesin sebelum membuat kacamata.
e: The optician checks my eyes with a machine before making the glasses.

t: Kacamata baru ini membuat tulisan di papan terlihat jelas lagi.
e: These new glasses make the writing on the board look clear again.

t: Bingkai kacamata itu cocok dengan bentuk wajah kamu.
e: That glasses frame suits the shape of your face.

t: Ayah memakai kacamata baca setiap kali membuka koran pagi.
e: Dad puts on his reading glasses every time he opens the morning paper.
g: Kacamata = glasses, literally kaca (glass) + mata (eye): kacamata baca = reading glasses.

t: Lensa kontak lebih praktis untuk olahraga, tapi mata saya cepat kering.
e: Contact lenses are more practical for sports, but my eyes dry out quickly.

t: Kacamata saya patah karena diduduki adik kecil saya kemarin.
e: My glasses broke because my little sibling sat on them yesterday.

t: Di optik itu, kacamata bisa selesai dalam waktu satu jam saja.
e: At that optical shop, glasses can be finished in just one hour.

t: Ukuran minus mata kiri dan kanan saya ternyata berbeda jauh.
e: It turns out the prescriptions of my left and right eyes differ a lot.

t: Dokter mata menyarankan saya mengistirahatkan mata setiap dua puluh menit.
e: The eye doctor advises me to rest my eyes every twenty minutes.

t: Kalau badan pegal dan meriang, orang Indonesia bilang sedang masuk angin.
e: When the body is achy and feverish, Indonesians say you have 'masuk angin'.
g: Masuk angin ('wind got in') = the classic catch-all unwellness: chills, bloating, fatigue. Untranslatable.

t: Nenek minta dikerok punggungnya setiap kali merasa masuk angin.
e: Grandma asks to have her back coin-rubbed every time she feels she has masuk angin.
g: Kerokan: rubbing a coin down the back until it stripes red — the beloved home cure for masuk angin.

t: Bekas kerokan di punggung ayah merah semua, katanya makin merah makin manjur.
e: The kerokan marks on Dad's back are all red; he says the redder, the more effective.

t: Setiap pagi ibu minum jamu kunyit asam buatan tetangga.
e: Every morning Mom drinks turmeric-tamarind jamu made by the neighbor.
g: Jamu = traditional herbal tonic (turmeric, ginger...): minum jamu = drink jamu, for health not taste.

t: Penjual jamu gendong masih lewat depan rumah kami setiap pagi.
e: The traveling jamu seller still passes in front of our house every morning.
g: Jamu gendong = jamu sold by a walking vendor carrying bottles in a back sling (gendong = carry on the back).

t: Kata nenek, wedang jahe hangat ampuh untuk menghangatkan badan saat hujan.
e: According to Grandma, warm ginger drink works wonders for warming the body when it rains.

t: Ibu mengoleskan minyak kayu putih di perut adik yang kembung.
e: Mom rubs cajuput oil on my little sibling's bloated tummy.
g: Minyak kayu putih = cajuput oil, the warm-smelling cure-all rubbed on every Indonesian child's belly.

t: Tukang urut langganan keluarga kami datang ke rumah setiap bulan.
e: Our family's regular massage man comes to the house every month.

t: Setelah diurut, kaki saya yang keseleo terasa jauh lebih enak.
e: After being massaged, my sprained foot feels much better.

t: Banyak orang percaya bawang merah bisa menurunkan demam anak kecil.
e: Many people believe shallots can bring down a small child's fever.

t: Minum air kelapa muda katanya bagus untuk meredakan panas dalam.
e: Drinking young coconut water is said to be good for soothing 'panas dalam'.
g: Panas dalam ('inner heat') = folk ailment behind sore throats and canker sores; cooled with kelapa muda.

t: Sehabis melahirkan, kakak saya minum jamu supaya badannya cepat pulih.
e: After giving birth, my older sister drinks jamu so her body recovers quickly.

t: Campuran madu dan jeruk nipis jadi andalan ibu untuk meredakan batuk.
e: A mix of honey and lime is Mom's go-to for easing a cough.

t: Meskipun modern, dokter kami tidak melarang kerokan asal kulit tidak terluka.
e: Even though he is modern, our doctor doesn't forbid kerokan as long as the skin isn't injured.
g: Asal = as long as (condition): asal kulit tidak terluka = as long as the skin isn't hurt.

t: Balsam hangat ini selalu ada di dalam tas nenek ke mana-mana.
e: This warming balm is always in Grandma's bag wherever she goes.

t: Kantor saya menanggung asuransi kesehatan untuk karyawan dan keluarganya.
e: My office covers health insurance for the employees and their families.

t: Sebelum pulang, saya harus menyelesaikan tagihan rumah sakit di kasir.
e: Before going home, I have to settle the hospital bill at the cashier.

t: Jangan membuang kuitansi obat karena kita memerlukannya untuk klaim asuransi.
e: Don't throw away the medicine receipts because we need them for the insurance claim.
g: Kuitansi = official receipt (from Dutch 'kwitantie'): minta kuitansi = ask for a receipt.

t: Pihak asuransi menolak klaim kami karena satu dokumen kurang lengkap.
e: The insurance company rejected our claim because one document was incomplete.

t: Biaya rawat inap tiga hari itu hampir sepuluh juta rupiah.
e: The cost of that three-day hospital stay is almost ten million rupiah.

t: Untung asuransi kantor menanggung sebagian besar biaya operasi suami saya.
e: Luckily the office insurance covers most of the cost of my husband's operation.

t: Petugas administrasi menjelaskan rincian tagihan sebelum kami membayar.
e: The administration officer explains the breakdown of the bill before we pay.

t: Saya mencicil sisa tagihan rumah sakit selama enam bulan.
e: I am paying off the rest of the hospital bill in installments over six months.
g: Mencicil = pay in installments: mencicil tagihan = pay the bill bit by bit.

t: Simpan semua hasil laboratorium dan surat dokter untuk berkas klaim.
e: Keep all the lab results and doctor's letters for the claim file.

t: Asuransi perjalanan menanggung biaya berobat saya waktu sakit di Bali.
e: The travel insurance covered my treatment costs when I was sick in Bali.

t: Sore ini kami akan menjenguk paman yang dirawat di rumah sakit.
e: This afternoon we are going to visit our uncle who is hospitalized.
g: Menjenguk = visit someone sick or a new baby — a real social duty: menjenguk paman = visit uncle.

t: Teman-teman kantor patungan membeli parsel buah untuk menjenguk Bu Sari.
e: The office friends chip in to buy a fruit basket for visiting Mrs. Sari.
g: Patungan = chip in together: patungan membeli parsel = pool money to buy a gift basket.

t: Jangan lupa membawakan bubur ayam kesukaannya waktu menjenguk kakek nanti.
e: Don't forget to bring his favorite chicken porridge when visiting Grandpa later.

t: Semoga cepat sembuh, ya, kabari kami kalau perlu bantuan apa pun.
e: Get well soon, okay? Let us know if you need any help at all.
g: Semoga cepat sembuh = get well soon, literally 'hopefully quickly recover' — the standard sick wish.

t: Ibu menitip salam dan doa untuk tantemu yang sedang sakit.
e: Mom sends her greetings and prayers for your aunt who is sick.

t: Kami bergantian menjaga nenek di rumah sakit selama seminggu penuh.
e: We take turns watching over Grandma at the hospital for a full week.

t: Setelah operasi, pasien hanya boleh dijenguk oleh dua orang saja.
e: After the operation, the patient may only be visited by just two people.

t: Grup keluarga langsung ramai begitu kabar opname kakek tersebar.
e: The family group chat got lively as soon as news of Grandpa's hospitalization spread.
g: Opname (from Dutch) = being admitted to hospital: kabar opname kakek = news of Grandpa's hospital stay.

t: Tetangga datang membawa sup hangat waktu anak saya sakit demam berdarah.
e: The neighbors came bringing warm soup when my child was sick with dengue fever.
g: Demam berdarah (DBD) = dengue fever, literally 'bleeding fever' — the rainy-season worry.

t: Jenguklah dia selagi masih dirawat, dia pasti senang melihat kalian.
e: Do visit him while he is still hospitalized; he will surely be happy to see you all.

t: Sepulang dari rumah sakit, ayah dilarang bekerja berat selama sebulan.
e: After coming home from the hospital, Dad is forbidden from doing heavy work for a month.

t: Sejak kuliah di Bandung, adik saya tinggal di kamar kos dekat kampus.
e: Since studying in Bandung, my younger sibling has lived in a boarding room near campus.
g: Kos = a rented room in a shared house, classic student housing: kamar kos = boarding room.

t: Setelah menikah, mereka pindah dari kamar kos ke rumah kontrakan dua kamar.
e: After getting married, they moved from a boarding room to a two-bedroom rented house.
g: Kontrakan = a whole house you rent, usually yearly; kos = just a room: rumah kontrakan = rented house.

t: Harga kos di dekat kantor baru saya ternyata mahal sekali.
e: The price of a room near my new office turns out to be really expensive.

t: Ibu kos saya baik; kalau saya telat membayar beberapa hari, dia tidak marah.
e: My landlady is kind; if I am a few days late paying, she does not get angry.
g: Ibu kos = the landlady who runs a boarding house: bayar ke ibu kos = pay the landlady.

t: Biaya kos saya sudah termasuk listrik dan air, jadi pengeluaran gampang dihitung.
e: My room fee already includes electricity and water, so expenses are easy to calculate.

t: Kontrakan kami dibayar per tahun, jadi kami harus menyiapkan uang besar sekaligus.
e: Our rented house is paid for per year, so we have to prepare a large sum at once.

t: Sebelum menandatangani kontrak, cek dulu apakah harganya termasuk air dan listrik.
e: Before signing the contract, first check whether the price includes water and electricity.

t: Teman sekamar saya di kos sering lupa membayar iuran kebersihan.
e: My roommate at the boarding house often forgets to pay the cleaning dues.
g: Iuran = a regular fee everyone pays into: iuran kebersihan = the cleaning dues.

t: Anak kos biasanya memasak sendiri di akhir bulan supaya lebih hemat.
e: Boarding-house kids usually cook for themselves at the end of the month to be more thrifty.
g: Anak kos = someone living in a kos — shorthand for a tight budget: masakan anak kos = cheap cooking.

t: Pemilik kontrakan menaikkan harga sewa lima persen mulai tahun depan.
e: The owner of the rented house is raising the rent five percent starting next year.

t: Kami masih mencari kontrakan yang dekat sekolah anak-anak dan pasar.
e: We are still looking for a rental house near the children's school and the market.

t: Daripada mengontrak terus, lebih baik uangnya dipakai untuk mencicil rumah kecil.
e: Rather than renting forever, it is better to use the money to pay for a small house in installments.

t: Bulan depan kontrak kos saya habis, dan saya belum tahu mau memperpanjang atau pindah.
e: Next month my room lease runs out, and I do not know yet whether I want to extend or move.

t: Listrik di rumah kami pakai token, jadi harus diisi sebelum habis.
e: The electricity at our house uses tokens, so it has to be topped up before it runs out.
g: Token = prepaid electricity credit: beli token listrik = buy a code and punch it into the meter.

t: Tengah malam meteran berbunyi, ternyata token listriknya hampir habis.
e: In the middle of the night the meter beeped; it turned out the electricity credit was almost gone.

t: Saya selalu membeli token listrik seratus ribu setiap awal bulan.
e: I always buy a hundred thousand worth of electricity credit at the start of each month.

t: Kalau mati lampu, kami menyalakan lilin dan mengobrol di teras.
e: When the power goes out, we light candles and chat on the porch.
g: Mati lampu = a power cut of any kind, not just the lamps: sedang mati lampu = the power is out.

t: Angka di meteran listrik dicatat petugas setiap tanggal dua puluh.
e: The reading on the electricity meter is recorded by an officer on the twentieth of every month.

t: Mati lampu di daerah kami biasanya sebentar saja, paling lama satu jam.
e: Power cuts in our area are usually only brief, one hour at most.

t: Tagihan listrik kantor naik terus karena AC menyala sampai malam.
e: The office electricity bill keeps going up because the AC stays on until night.

t: Nomor meteran harus dimasukkan waktu membeli token lewat aplikasi.
e: The meter number has to be entered when buying electricity credit through the app.

t: Rumah kontrakan kami yang lama masih memakai meteran bulanan, bukan token.
e: Our old rented house still uses a monthly meter, not tokens.

t: Kulkas sempat mati waktu mati lampu kemarin, untung makanannya belum rusak.
e: The fridge went off for a while during yesterday's power cut; luckily the food had not spoiled.

t: Kata ayah, setrika dan pemanas air paling banyak memakan token listrik.
e: According to dad, the iron and the water heater eat up the most electricity credit.

t: Kami sengaja memilih AC baru yang katanya lebih irit listrik.
e: We deliberately chose a new AC that is said to use less electricity.

t: Waktu token habis tengah malam, minimarket dekat rumah jadi penyelamat.
e: When the electricity credit ran out in the middle of the night, the minimart near the house became the savior.

t: Air PAM di kompleks kami sering mati siang hari, jadi kami menampung air di ember.
e: The city water in our housing complex often goes off during the day, so we store water in buckets.
g: PAM = the city water utility: air PAM = tap water, used for washing rather than drinking.

t: Tagihan air PAM bulan ini lebih besar karena ada pipa bocor.
e: This month's city water bill is bigger because there was a leaking pipe.

t: Untuk minum kami pakai air galon; air PAM hanya untuk mandi dan mencuci.
e: For drinking we use gallon water; the tap water is only for bathing and washing.
g: Galon = the big 19-liter water bottle at home: air galon = drinking water from the dispenser.

t: Kalau air galon habis, tinggal telepon warung, nanti diantar sampai dapur.
e: When the gallon water runs out, just phone the corner shop, and it gets delivered right to the kitchen.

t: Satu galon isi ulang di depot dekat rumah harganya enam ribu.
e: One refill gallon at the depot near the house costs six thousand.
g: Isi ulang = refill: galon isi ulang = a refilled gallon from the water depot, cheaper than branded.

t: Abang galon langsung mengangkat galon kosong dan memasang yang baru.
e: The water delivery guy immediately lifted the empty gallon and installed the new one.

t: Pemakaian air kami bulan kemarin tinggi, mungkin karena banyak tamu menginap.
e: Our water usage last month was high, maybe because many guests stayed over.

t: Di kompleks kami, air PAM mengalir kencang hanya pagi dan malam hari.
e: In our complex, the city water flows strongly only in the morning and at night.

t: Ibu menyuruh kami menghemat air karena musim kemarau masih panjang.
e: Mom told us to save water because the dry season is still long.

t: Mereka membeli motor baru dengan DP tiga juta dan cicilan dua tahun.
e: They bought a new motorbike with a three-million down payment and two years of installments.
g: DP (say de-pe) = down payment: DP tiga juta = a three-million down payment. Also called uang muka.

t: Cicilan motor itu delapan ratus ribu per bulan, belum termasuk asuransi.
e: The installments for that motorbike are eight hundred thousand a month, not yet including insurance.
g: Cicilan = an installment; mencicil = pay bit by bit: cicilan dua tahun = two years of installments.

t: Kami menunda membeli kulkas baru karena masih ada dua cicilan berjalan.
e: We are putting off buying a new fridge because there are still two installment plans running.

t: Kalau uang mukanya lebih besar, cicilan bulanannya jadi lebih ringan.
e: If the down payment is bigger, the monthly installments become lighter.

t: Sisa cicilan rumah kami masih delapan tahun, pelan-pelan pasti lunas.
e: The remainder of our house installments is still eight years; slowly but surely it will be paid off.
g: Lunas = fully paid off: cicilannya sudah lunas = the installments are all paid.

t: Uang bonus akhir tahun langsung dia pakai untuk melunasi cicilan HP.
e: He immediately used his year-end bonus money to pay off his phone installments.

t: Jangan sampai menunggak cicilan, karena dendanya lumayan besar.
e: Do not let yourself fall behind on the installments, because the fine is quite big.
g: Menunggak = to fall behind on payments: menunggak cicilan = to miss installments.

t: Sebelum mengambil cicilan baru, hitung dulu semua pengeluaran bulananmu.
e: Before taking on a new installment plan, first count up all your monthly expenses.

t: Teman kantor saya menyesal mengambil cicilan mobil sebelum gajinya naik.
e: My office friend regrets taking on car installments before his salary went up.

t: Toko itu menawarkan cicilan tanpa bunga untuk pembelian di atas satu juta.
e: That store offers installments without interest for purchases above one million.
g: Bunga = flower AND interest: cicilan tanpa bunga = zero-interest installments.

t: DP rumah biasanya paling sedikit sepuluh persen dari harga rumahnya.
e: The down payment on a house is usually at least ten percent of the house price.

t: Arisan ibu-ibu di kompleks kami berkumpul setiap tanggal lima belas.
e: The neighborhood mothers' arisan in our complex gathers on the fifteenth of every month.
g: Arisan = a rotating savings club — all pay in, one takes the pot: ikut arisan = join one.

t: Nama ibu keluar waktu arisan dikocok, lumayan untuk membayar uang sekolah adik.
e: Mom's name came out when the arisan was drawn — helpful for paying my younger sibling's school fees.
g: Dikocok = shaken up and drawn by lot: nama ibu keluar = mom's name came out, she wins this round.

t: Banyak orang ikut arisan supaya bisa menabung sambil tetap bertemu teman-teman.
e: Many people join an arisan so they can save money while still meeting their friends.

t: Iuran arisan kantor kami dua ratus ribu, ditarik setiap tanggal gajian.
e: Our office arisan dues are two hundred thousand, collected every payday.

t: Ibu memakai uang arisan untuk membayar DP kulkas baru di toko elektronik.
e: Mom used her arisan money to pay the down payment on a new fridge at the electronics store.

t: Kalau dapat giliran pertama, uang arisan terasa seperti pinjaman tanpa bunga.
e: If you get the first turn, the arisan money feels like an interest-free loan.
g: Giliran = your turn in a rotation: dapat giliran pertama = get the first turn.

t: Setiap arisan selesai, ibu-ibu masih duduk lama membahas harga sembako.
e: Every time the arisan is over, the mothers still sit around a long time discussing staple food prices.
g: Sembako = the nine basic goods (rice, oil, sugar, and so on): harga sembako = staple prices.

t: Gaji pertama saya dulu di bawah UMR, tapi pengalamannya sangat berharga.
e: My first salary back then was below the regional minimum wage, but the experience was very valuable.
g: UMR = the regional minimum wage: di bawah UMR = below minimum wage.

t: UMR di Jakarta lebih tinggi daripada di kota kecil, tapi biaya hidupnya juga tinggi.
e: The minimum wage in Jakarta is higher than in small towns, but the cost of living is also high.

t: Setiap akhir tahun, pemerintah daerah mengumumkan UMR baru untuk tahun berikutnya.
e: Every end of year, the regional government announces the new minimum wage for the following year.

t: Gaji saya cukup untuk kebutuhan bulanan, sisanya saya tabung sedikit-sedikit.
e: My salary is enough for monthly needs; the rest I save bit by bit.

t: Gaji di kantor kami cair setiap tanggal dua puluh lima, langsung dipotong iuran.
e: The salary at our office comes through on the twenty-fifth, with dues deducted right away.
g: Cair, literally liquid = money comes through: gajinya sudah cair = the salary has landed.

t: Perusahaan kami menaikkan gaji sekali setahun, biasanya sesudah penilaian kerja.
e: Our company raises salaries once a year, usually after the performance review.

t: Selain gaji pokok, dia menerima uang makan dan uang transportasi.
e: Besides his base salary, he receives meal money and transport money.
g: Gaji pokok = base salary, before the extras: selain gaji pokok = on top of base salary.

t: Kata teman saya, gaji di pabrik baru itu sedikit di atas UMR.
e: According to my friend, the pay at that new factory is slightly above minimum wage.

t: Setelah tiga tahun bekerja di sana, akhirnya gajinya naik cukup besar.
e: After working there for three years, his salary finally went up quite a lot.

t: Gaji suaminya masuk ke rekening bersama untuk kebutuhan rumah tangga.
e: Her husband's salary goes into a joint account for household needs.

t: Kami membagi gaji ke tiga pos: kebutuhan, tabungan, dan hiburan.
e: We divide the salary into three categories: needs, savings, and fun.
g: Pos = a budget category: pos tabungan = the savings slot in the family budget.

t: Kakak saya hemat sekali; sepatu kerjanya dipakai sampai lima tahun.
e: My older sibling is really frugal; their work shoes get worn for up to five years.
g: Hemat = careful with money, boros = wasteful — everyday opposites: dia hemat sekali = very frugal.

t: Saya gampang boros kalau lapar; semua jajanan di pasar ingin saya beli.
e: I easily overspend when I am hungry; I want to buy every snack in the market.

t: Bulan ini kami harus lebih hemat karena ada biaya sekolah anak.
e: This month we have to be more frugal because there are the children's school costs.

t: Membawa bekal dari rumah jauh lebih hemat daripada membeli makan siang setiap hari.
e: Bringing a packed lunch from home is far more economical than buying lunch every day.

t: Dia kelihatan boros, padahal barang-barang mahalnya dibeli waktu diskon besar.
e: He looks like a big spender, even though his expensive things were bought during big sales.

t: Kata ibu, hemat itu bukan pelit, tapi tahu mana yang penting.
e: According to mom, being frugal is not being stingy, it is knowing what matters.
g: Pelit = stingy; hemat = sensibly careful: hemat itu bukan pelit = frugal is not stingy.

t: Langganan aplikasi yang jarang dipakai pelan-pelan membuat kita boros.
e: App subscriptions that are rarely used slowly make us wasteful.

t: Supaya hemat bensin, dia berangkat lebih pagi dan menghindari jam macet.
e: To save on fuel, he leaves earlier and avoids rush hour.

t: Kebiasaan kecil seperti mematikan lampu siang hari lama-lama terasa di tagihan.
e: Small habits like turning off the lights during the day eventually show in the bill.

t: Belanja bulanan kami biasanya di pasar dan supermarket dekat rumah.
e: Our monthly shopping is usually at the market and the supermarket near the house.
g: Belanja bulanan = the big monthly shop: uang belanja = the household shopping money.

t: Ibu selalu menulis daftar dulu supaya belanja bulanan tidak ada yang terlewat.
e: Mom always writes a list first so nothing in the monthly shop gets missed.

t: Beras, minyak goreng, dan sabun selalu ada di daftar belanja bulanan kami.
e: Rice, cooking oil, and soap are always on our monthly shopping list.

t: Belanja bulanan tanpa daftar ujung-ujungnya penuh barang yang tidak penting.
e: A monthly shop without a list ends up full of unimportant stuff.
g: Ujung-ujungnya = it always ends up: ujung-ujungnya boros = in the end you overspend.

t: Kami membandingkan harga di dua supermarket sebelum belanja bulanan yang besar.
e: We compare prices at two supermarkets before the big monthly shop.

t: Belanja sembako di pasar pagi lebih murah, tapi harus pintar menawar.
e: Shopping for staples at the morning market is cheaper, but you have to be good at bargaining.

t: Anak-anak senang ikut belanja bulanan karena boleh memilih satu camilan.
e: The kids love coming along on the monthly shop because they may pick one snack.

t: Sejak harga-harga naik, uang belanja bulanan kami sering kurang di minggu terakhir.
e: Since prices went up, our monthly shopping money often falls short in the last week.

t: Ayah kebagian tugas mengangkat semua kantong belanja dari mobil ke dapur.
e: Dad gets the job of carrying all the shopping bags from the car to the kitchen.

t: Harga cabai naik lagi, Bu? Rasanya kemarin masih setengah dari ini.
e: Chili prices are up again, ma'am? I feel like yesterday it was still half this much.
g: Chili prices are national small talk — they jump constantly: harga cabai naik lagi = up again.

t: Dulu lima puluh ribu cukup untuk seminggu, sekarang dua hari saja sudah habis.
e: Fifty thousand used to be enough for a week; now it is gone in just two days.

t: Menjelang hari raya, harga daging dan telur biasanya naik lebih dulu.
e: In the run-up to the big holiday, meat and egg prices usually go up first.

t: Ibu-ibu di warung sayur setiap pagi membahas harga minyak goreng.
e: The women at the vegetable stall discuss cooking-oil prices every morning.

t: Katanya harga gas tiga kilo mau naik lagi bulan depan.
e: They say the price of the three-kilo gas canister is going to go up again next month.

t: Harga kopi di kafe dekat kantor naik, jadi kami kembali ke kopi saset.
e: The coffee price at the cafe near the office went up, so we went back to sachet coffee.

t: Waktu semua harga naik begini, warung kecil bingung mau menaikkan harga atau tidak.
e: When all prices rise like this, small food stalls are not sure whether to raise prices or not.

t: Setiap harga BBM naik, ongkos angkot ikut naik pelan-pelan.
e: Every time fuel prices rise, minibus fares slowly rise along with them.
g: BBM = bahan bakar minyak, fuel: harga BBM naik = fuel prices went up — everything follows.

t: Untung gaji naik sedikit tahun ini, jadi kenaikan harga tidak terlalu terasa.
e: Luckily salaries went up a little this year, so the price increases are not felt too much.

t: Berapa ongkos angkot dari sini sampai terminal, Bang?
e: How much is the minibus fare from here to the terminal, sir?
g: Ongkos = fare, the cost of getting somewhere: ongkos angkot = the minibus fare.

t: Saya memilih toko yang lebih jauh karena ongkirnya gratis.
e: I chose the store that is farther away because its shipping is free.
g: Ongkir = ongkos kirim, the delivery fee; plain ongkos is a transport fare: gratis ongkir = free shipping.

t: Ongkir ke luar pulau bisa lebih mahal daripada harga barangnya sendiri.
e: Shipping to another island can be more expensive than the price of the item itself.

t: Kalau belanja di atas seratus ribu, aplikasi itu memberi gratis ongkir.
e: If you shop above one hundred thousand, that app gives free shipping.

t: Dulu ongkos bus ke kampung dua puluh ribu, sekarang hampir dua kali lipat.
e: The bus fare to the village used to be twenty thousand; now it is almost double.
g: Dua kali lipat = double: hampir dua kali lipat = almost twice as much.

t: Sopir travel menaikkan ongkos waktu musim liburan, katanya harga bensin juga naik.
e: The shuttle drivers raise fares during holiday season; they say fuel prices have gone up too.

t: Penjual online biasanya menulis bahwa harga belum termasuk ongkir.
e: Online sellers usually write that the price does not yet include shipping.

t: Saya menggabungkan dua pesanan dalam satu keranjang supaya ongkirnya lebih murah.
e: I combined two orders into one cart so the shipping would be cheaper.

t: Ongkos parkir langganan di gedung kantor dipotong langsung dari gaji bulanan.
e: The monthly parking fee at the office building is deducted straight from the monthly salary.

t: Kami patungan membeli kado pernikahan untuk teman satu tim di kantor.
e: We chipped in together to buy a wedding gift for a teammate at the office.
g: Patungan = to chip in together: kami patungan = we split the cost.

t: Untuk acara makan-makan akhir bulan, setiap orang patungan lima puluh ribu.
e: For the end-of-month get-together meal, each person chips in fifty thousand.

t: Anak-anak kompleks patungan membeli jaring baru untuk lapangan voli.
e: The kids in the complex chipped in to buy a new net for the volleyball court.

t: Daripada sewa mobil sendiri-sendiri, lebih murah kalau kita patungan satu mobil besar.
e: Rather than renting cars separately, it is cheaper if we all chip in for one big car.

t: Keluarga besar kami patungan membayar biaya rumah sakit kakek bulan lalu.
e: Our extended family chipped in to pay grandpa's hospital costs last month.

t: Kalau bensinnya patungan, perjalanan mudik naik mobil terasa lebih ringan.
e: If the fuel is split between everyone, the drive home for the holidays feels much lighter.

t: Uang patungan kemarin masih sisa tiga puluh ribu, mau dipakai untuk apa?
e: There is still thirty thousand left from yesterday's pooled money — what shall we use it for?

t: Target kami tahun ini menabung sepuluh juta untuk DP rumah kecil.
e: Our target this year is to save ten million for the down payment on a small house.

t: Sejak kecil, ayah mengajari saya menyisihkan uang jajan ke celengan.
e: Since I was little, dad taught me to set aside pocket money into a piggy bank.
g: Celengan = a piggy bank: menyisihkan uang ke celengan = set money aside in the piggy bank.

t: Dia menabung di rekening terpisah supaya uangnya tidak gampang terpakai.
e: She saves in a separate account so the money does not get spent by accident.

t: Kami menabung sedikit demi sedikit untuk biaya kuliah anak nanti.
e: We are saving little by little for the children's future college costs.
g: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little: menabung sedikit demi sedikit = save bit by bit.

t: Uang receh di toples itu ternyata cukup untuk membeli kipas angin.
e: The loose change in that jar turned out to be enough to buy a fan.

t: Setiap gajian, dia langsung memindahkan uang tabungan ke rekening lain.
e: Every payday, he immediately moves his savings money to another account.

t: Tabungan liburan kami sempat terpakai waktu motor tiba-tiba masuk bengkel.
e: Our holiday savings did get used at one point when the motorbike suddenly went into the repair shop.

t: Menabung di awal bulan lebih mudah daripada menunggu sisa uang di akhir bulan.
e: Saving at the start of the month is easier than waiting for leftover money at the end of the month.

t: Nenek lebih percaya menyimpan uangnya di lemari daripada di bank.
e: Grandma trusts keeping her money in the wardrobe more than in the bank.

t: Saldo dompet digital saya tinggal lima ribu, nanti saya isi di minimarket.
e: My digital wallet balance is down to five thousand; I will top it up later at the minimart.
g: Isi saldo = top up a balance: saya isi di minimarket = I will top it up at the minimart.

t: Sekarang mengisi saldo bisa lewat aplikasi bank, tidak perlu antre di konter.
e: Nowadays topping up the balance can be done through the bank app; no need to queue at a counter.

t: Tukang parkir di pasar sekarang juga menerima pembayaran lewat dompet digital.
e: The parking attendants at the market now also accept payment through digital wallets.
g: Tukang = the ... guy, by trade: tukang parkir = parking attendant, tukang galon = the water guy.

t: Saya mengisi saldo dua ratus ribu setiap minggu khusus untuk ongkos ojek online.
e: I top up two hundred thousand every week just for online motorbike-taxi fares.

t: Membayar pakai dompet digital sering dapat potongan, tapi hati-hati jadi boros.
e: Paying with a digital wallet often gets you a discount, but be careful you do not turn wasteful.

t: Ibu akhirnya mau belajar memakai dompet digital supaya gampang membayar uang sekolah adik.
e: Mom is finally willing to learn to use a digital wallet so paying my younger sibling's school fees is easy.

t: Waktu sinyal hilang, dompet digital tidak bisa dibuka; untung masih ada uang tunai.
e: When the signal disappeared, the digital wallet could not be opened; luckily there was still cash.

t: Anak muda sekarang jarang membawa dompet karena semua pembayaran lewat HP.
e: Young people these days rarely carry a wallet because all payments go through their phones.

t: Mengisi saldo di minimarket biasanya kena biaya tambahan seribu rupiah.
e: Topping up a balance at the minimart usually incurs an extra fee of one thousand rupiah.
g: Kena biaya = get charged a fee: kena biaya seribu = charged one thousand.
